summary:
Nevşehir province operates under Turkey's national legal framework. No province-specific ordinance, incident or court decision has been recorded for Nevşehir; the sources supporting this record are national in scope, and the assessment below is the national picture as encountered in a tourism district of Cappadocia, where a tourism economy sits alongside regional conservatism.

Homosexuality has not been a criminal offence since the Ottoman penal code of 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988. No comprehensive law prohibits discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, and same-sex marriage is not recognised. Openly LGBTI people are barred from military service: conscripts who declare their homosexuality are classed under a definition of homosexuality as a 'psychosexual illness', must provide photographic proof, and risk their 'unfit report' being made public.

Since 2015 local authorities have repeatedly banned and forcibly dispersed Pride marches, with police using water cannon and tear gas on the 2015 and 2016 Istanbul parades. Amnesty International's Türkiye country report (Report 2025/26) records that in June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the Istanbul LGBTI and Trans pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful use of force, over 90 people were arbitrarily detained, and prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end.

Amnesty also records that three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people were made public during 2025. The packages would criminalize expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible, and they were ultimately not submitted to parliament. Press reports in early 2026 said the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex'; the provision was not included in the year's judicial reform package.

In December 2025 an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association, ruling that it had shared 'obscene' images incompatible with 'society's moral values' that could 'encourage or promote' LGBTI identities.
tangentialFactors:
Cappadocia's tourism economy draws international visitors year-round, but the sources record no Nevşehir-specific incident, enforcement action or local ordinance affecting LGBT or trans travellers. The province's conservatism is noted in the record without documented consequence for visitors.

The national pattern of Pride bans and dispersals since 2015 has centred on Istanbul and other large cities; no Nevşehir Pride event or local ban is documented in the sources.

outOfScopeNotes:
Whether any of the three 2025 draft packages or the early-2026 proposal has since been enacted is unresolved in the sources.

No Nevşehir-specific enforcement data, local police practice or provincial court decision on LGBT or trans matters is sourced; the record rests on national material.
